title: The Old Dark House
byline: Universal Pictures / James Whale, 1932 — copyright L 3321 not renewed; public domain since expiry of first 28-year term

evidence.note: Renewed. Catalog of Copyright Entries, Third Series, Vol. 14, Parts 12-13 (Jan-Dec 1960), renewal list: 'OLD DARK HOUSE, a photoplay in nine reels by Universal Pictures Corp. (c) 12Oct32; LP3321. Universal Pictures Co., Inc. (PWH); 17Jun60; R258433.' A renewed 1932 film is protected for 95 years from publication: it enters the US public domain on 1 January 2028.
evidence.source: Catalog of Copyright Entries, Third Series, Vol. 14, Parts 12-13 (1960)

evidence.note: Universal Pictures Corporation registered the film as 'The Old Dark House U.P. 9 Reels', registration L 3321, application received 1932-10-13, first published 1932-10-12. Establishes renewal window as calendar years 1959–1960.
evidence.source: U.S. Copyright Office Public Records System, card catalog record for L 3321

evidence.note: The recorded soundtrack (dialogue and music) is part of the 1932 film, whose copyright was renewed in 1960 (R258433). It is protected until the film enters the US public domain on 1 January 2028.
evidence.source: Catalog of Copyright Entries, Third Series, Vol. 14, Parts 12-13 (1960)

evidence.note: Based on J.B. Priestley's novel Benighted, first published in 1927 (UK) and in 1928 in the US as The Old Dark House. Works published in 1928 entered the US public domain on 1 January 2024, so the novel is free; material that exists only in the 1932 film is not free until 2028.

An Internet Archive item ('the_old_dark_house', Community Video collection, uploaded August 2026) contains a 1080p BluRay H.264 file (399.6 MB) and a Matroska file (6.5 GB), format and size strongly indicating a commercial Blu-ray source. Under Bridgeman v. Corel and Feist, a faithful restoration scan adds no new US copyright in the underlying footage. However: (1) any new supplemental material included on a commercial disc (liner notes, commentary tracks, bonus features) carries its own copyright; (2) circumventing copy protection on a physical Blu-ray disc is independently prohibited under 17 U.S.C. § 1201 regardless of whether the underlying film is public domain. A free, explicitly public-domain copy (Archive.org item TheOldDarkHouse, marked CC Public Domain Mark 1.0, uploaded 2018) is available and avoids both concerns.
evidence.source: Internet Archive item the_old_dark_house, page fetched 2026-10-06

editorial:
Universal Pictures released The Old Dark House in October 1932, produced under James Whale's direction with a cast that includes Boris Karloff as the mute, brutish manservant Morgan, Charles Laughton, Raymond Massey, Gloria Stuart, and Melvyn Douglas. Universal registered the copyright (LP3321, published 12 October 1932) and renewed it on 17 June 1960 (R258433), so the film stays protected in the US until it enters the public domain on 1 January 2028. Curtis Harrington discovered a surviving print in Universal's vaults in 1968 and persuaded George Eastman House to finance restoration of the film. Some online copies are labelled public domain; for this film that label is wrong until 2028, so screening, streaming or redistributing it needs permission from the rights holder until then.

The rights trap to avoid is the Blu-ray restoration circuit. A 1080p Blu-ray–sourced file (6.5 GB Matroska) circulates on Archive.org as of 2026, indicating that a commercial restoration has been pressed to disc. A faithful scan of a public-domain film adds no new US copyright under Feist and Bridgeman v. Corel, but the physical disc is separately shielded by DMCA anti-circumvention (17 U.S.C. § 1201), and any bonus material on the disc carries its own copyright. Use the 2018 Archive.org copy (identifier TheOldDarkHouse, explicitly marked Public Domain Mark 1.0) rather than a disc rip. One further open question: the 1928 US copyright on Priestley's source novel (registration A 1018678) may or may not have been renewed in 1956; anyone planning a new adaptation that draws on the novel beyond the film should verify the 1956 CCE book renewal records before proceeding.
faq: Can I screen, stream, or redistribute this film?

Not yet. Universal renewed the copyright on 17 June 1960 (R258433), so the film is protected in the US until 1 January 2028. Some online copies are labelled public domain; that label is wrong for this film until then.
Can I write a new adaptation drawing on the Priestley source novel?

Yes, from the novel. Priestley's Benighted (US edition 1928, as The Old Dark House) has been public domain in the US since 1 January 2024. Just don't copy material that exists only in the 1932 film before 2028.
